assessment: The thing every cycle since c-0009 has been waiting on happened, and it happened while nobody was watching: the ZoltarLead courier ran. Four receipts today, agent_id zoltarlead/courier, no model in the loop - 88899a3 carrying all five stranded order files plus cycles c-0008 through c-0013 after 46.9 to 48.9 hours on a disk nobody fetched, then 2a1c797, then a deliberate-looking failure against an unresolvable remote that wrote its receipt anyway, then b35437f at 22:12:25Z, ten minutes and one second after the previous run, unattended, observed from inside this fire. That last one is the only clause of the acceptance that could not have been faked by a person standing at the machine, and it is the one that matters. This board has carried its first real sha; the five-day split-brain named in handoff-04 is closed at the carrier layer, and origin/main here finally reads a246ccf instead of a3ad2ff. What it has not done is deliver anything, and the distinction c-0013 insisted on keeping sharp - dispatched is not delivered - now needs one more word: committed is not delivered either. The executors on ZoltarOne and ZoltarGenesis pull origin main and read the working tree, so every file the courier just landed is invisible to them, and the order that would fix exactly that - t-20260908-executor-dispatch-branch, which Andrew already approved two days ago - is itself one of the files on fleet/dispatch. It cannot deliver itself. That is a closed loop, not a queue, and the only act that opens it is a trunk act, which is Andrew's by hard floor at every autonomy level. Behind the loop sit the F-ZS-5 probe, which is the sole instrument that can distinguish a dead ZoltarOne from a misdirected executor after 72 hours of silence, and c-0002.1, whose 1-minute-bar window is 5.28 days out and irreversible. The build itself did not move and is not the subject: gate amber on the same five blocker contract tests stale since 2026-09-02. One thing arrived from outside - ZoltarStar's join message, over OneDrive alone, which proves that leg one-way and leaves F-ZS-1 exactly where it was.

The carrier gap that stranded it is now closed: the courier committed it at 88899a3 and is firing unattended. The remaining gap is one hop and it is a closed loop. run-order.ps1 on ZoltarOne and ZoltarGenesis pulls origin main --ff-only and reads orders/<node>/ from the working tree; everything the courier landed is on origin/fleet/dispatch. t-20260908-executor-dispatch-branch, approved by Andrew 2026-09-08, is the order that would teach them to read that ref, and it is committed only to that ref. No agent on this fleet may open the loop, because trunk is Andrew's - hard floor at L0 through L3.

items.title: F-ZS-4: the nvme tag has never been emitted by any node in this fleet, and routing is about to start depending on tags.
items.why: ZoltarStar reports derive_tags comparing the bus field to the integer 17 while every node card records the string 'NVMe'; three of four nodes have NVMe disks and none has ever carried the tag. This was inert while nothing routed. Spec section 4a routes a 'for: auto' task by matching requires against fleet_live.tags, and dispatch just became real, so an empty tag set stops being cosmetic: a router asking for fast local I/O cannot distinguish 'no node has NVMe' from 'this was never measurable' - the null-input-becomes-a-default failure rules.md rev 4 names. Raised 2026-09-08; its message only reached this clone today, and it had no home on this board until now.
items.acceptance: The comparison is quoted from source with file and line; either a node whose card records NVMe carries the tag in fleet_live.tags, or the finding is refuted in writing with the quoted line. No fleet card is hand-edited to add the tag.
